decisions.reason: This is a generic utility with limited dependence on the firm's regulated-energy knowledge base, so its absorptive-capacity advantage is weak and management would likely redeploy effort to more distinctive platform products.

An Austrian gas grid fee database is closely related to the firm's existing regulatory data and analytical capabilities, so it can learn and improve it efficiently even if the niche is relatively small.

Peak load window determination fits the firm's core strengths in energy calculations, compliance support, and operational web services, giving it strong scope to refine the offer from customer feedback.
An end-customer tariff database directly builds on the firm's long-developed data assets and software model and supports its move toward scalable SaaS and modular information services.

Although the firm can deliver custom web services, a standalone custom offering is less aligned with its shift toward standardized modular SaaS, so management is likely to phase it out as a distinct market product.

A postal code lookup service is highly commoditized and only weakly tied to the firm's specialist energy-market knowledge, making it a poor use of development capacity compared with more core products.
